entities.summary:
Gunderic, King of the Hasding Vandals from 407 CE and then King of the Vandals and Alans from 418 CE until his death in 428 CE, was a pivotal figure in the tumultuous fifth-century transformations of the Western Roman Empire. His reign witnessed the consolidation of diverse Germanic tribes into a formidable Vandalic power, whose relentless westward and southward migrations profoundly destabilized Roman control over Gaul and the Iberian Peninsula. Gunderic's strategic leadership and military prowess were instrumental in establishing a significant barbarian presence within the Roman imperium, fundamentally reshaping the geopolitical landscape of Late Antiquity.

Following the momentous Crossing of the Rhine in 406 CE, Gunderic led the Hasding Vandals through Gaul, eventually entering Hispania in 409 CE alongside the Suebi and Alans. For nearly two decades, his forces engaged in a complex series of conflicts and alliances with other barbarian groups and the embattled Roman authorities. After the death of the Alan king Attaces in 418 CE during a Visigothic campaign, Gunderic absorbed the remaining Alans, uniting the two peoples under his crown. He subsequently expanded Vandalic influence across Baetica, Lusitania, and Cartagena, culminating in the significant sack of Cartagena in 425 CE, which provided his burgeoning fleet with access to the Mediterranean and its vital trade routes.
